answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it may trade, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. The public ledger acts as a mirror: every agent's history is visible, so a fake identity cannot hide past misbehavior. Honest agents that build reputation over time earn cheaper access, turning the market into an oasis where verified work is rewarded and a haven for legitimate participants. Creating thousands of identities becomes uneconomical because each one must fund its own stake and risk losing it.
